items.blurb: Grafana Labs has released Tempo 3.1, the first minor update to the 3.0 architecture.

items.title: What Deleting Rows Does to a Table
items.blurb: I deleted half of a 2M-row table and the file stayed at 137 MB, through DELETE and through VACUUM. Only VACUUM FULL brought it to 68 MB. Plus DELETE against TRUNCATE, and what fillfactor does to updates.

items.title: Why Setting archive_command to /bin/true Can Lose Data
items.blurb: Setting archive_command to /bin/true can silently lose PostgreSQL data. In this blog post, Shaun Thomas shows how WAL, checkpoints, and PITR work, and what a missing segment does.

items.title: PgBouncer vs. Amazon RDS Proxy: How the Two Poolers Differ
items.blurb: Compare Amazon RDS Proxy and PgBouncer for PostgreSQL connection pooling on AWS. This post explains how each pooler handles pooling modes, authentication, failover, and session-state pinning, and gives you a framework to choose between a…

items.title: How TABLESAMPLE Picks Rows
items.blurb: TABLESAMPLE picks addresses, not rows: SYSTEM samples come in bundles, BERNOULLI with REPEATABLE drifts after an UPDATE, and a hashed key gives you the same rows tomorrow.

items.title: Put an agent to work on your Postgres database. It's free
items.blurb: Download rdst for macOS or Linux and start understanding, diagnosing, and speeding up your database queries.
